akhfash:54-54.t: He said: ﴿وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ وَٱلنُّجُومَ مُسَخَّرَاتٍ بِأَمْرِهِ﴾: this is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to His words ﴿خَلَقَ ٱلسَمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ﴾, i.e. "and He created ﴿الشَمْسَ والقَمَرَ﴾".

akhfash:56-56.t:
He said: ﴿إِنَّ رَحْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾. He made ﴿قَرِيب﴾ masculine although it is an adjective (ṣifa) of "الرحمة" (mercy, feminine). This is like the Arabs' saying "رِيحٌ خَريقٌ" (a violent wind), "مِلْحَفَةٌ جَديدٌ" (a new wrap) and "شاةٌ سَدِيسٌ" (a ewe in its sixth year). Or, if you wish, you may say: the explanation of "الرحمة" here is rain and the like; that is why it is made masculine, just as He said ﴿وَإِن كَانَ طَآئِفَةٌ مِّنكُمْ آمَنُواْ﴾ and used the masculine because He meant "people". Or, if you wish, you may treat it like some of the feminine nouns that they make masculine, as in the poet's words [in the mutaqārib metre, and it is the thirty-first poetic witness]:
[فَلا مِزْنَةٌ وَدَقَتْ وَدْقَها] * وَلا أَرْضُ* أَبْقَلَ إِبْقَالها
(No rain-cloud poured down its rain as it did, and no land put forth herbage as it did.)

akhfash:57-57.t:
He said: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُرْسِلُ ٱلرِّيَاحَ بُشْراً بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ﴾, because it is the plural of "النَشُور"; you say "رِيحٌ نَشُور" and "رياحٌ نُشُر". Some read "نَشْرا", from "نَشَرها" "نَشْراً" (He spread them out, a spreading).
And He said at the beginning of this sura ﴿كِتَابٌ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ﴾ [2] ﴿لِتُنذِرَ بِهِ﴾ [2] ﴿فَلاَ يَكُنْ فِي صَدْرِكَ حَرَجٌ مِّنْهُ﴾ [2]: this is how it is interpreted, by way of advancing and postponing (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr, i.e. inversion of order). There is much like this in the Book of Allah. He said ﴿ٱذْهَب بِّكِتَابِي هَـٰذَا فَأَلْقِهْ إِلَيْهِمْ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ فَٱنْظُرْ مَاذَا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾, and the meaning — and Allah knows best — is ﴿فَٱنْظُرْ مَاذَا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ ﴿ثُمَّ تَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ﴾. And in the Book of Allah: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ إِلاَّ رِجَالاً نُّوحِيۤ إِلَيْهِمْ فَٱسْأَلُواْ أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ إِن كُنْتُم لاَ تَعْلَمُونَ بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ وَٱلزُّبُرِ﴾, and the meaning — and Allah knows best — is ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ إِلاَّ رِجَالاً نُّوحِيۤ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ ﴿بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ وَٱلزُّبُرِ﴾ ﴿فَٱسْأَلُواْ أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ﴾ ﴿إِن كُنْتُم لاَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾. And in "Ḥā-Mīm al-Muʾmin": ﴿فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُم بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ فَرِحُواْ بِمَا عِندَهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ﴾, and the meaning — and Allah knows best — is ﴿فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُم بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ ﴿مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ﴾ ﴿فَرِحُواْ بِمَا عِندَهُمْ﴾. Some said that ﴿فَرِحُوا بِما﴾ is ﴿عِنْدَهُم مِنَ الِعلْم﴾, i.e. they had "knowledge" which was in fact ignorance. Advancing and postponing of this kind is frequent in the speech of the Arabs and in poetry. A man writes: "أَمّا بَعْدُ حَفِظَكَ اللهُ وَعافاكَ فإِنّي كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْكَ" (As for what follows — may Allah preserve you and keep you well — I have written to you); his words "فَإِنِّي" are attached to "أَمَّا بَعْدُ" — it is really "أَمَّا بَعْدُ فإِنّي" — and between them, as you see, there is other speech. The poet said [in the kāmil metre, and it is the two hundred and eighth poetic witness]:
خَيْرٌ مِنَ القَوْمِ العُصاةِ أَمِيرَهُم * يا قومُ فاستَحْيُوا النِسَاءُ الجُلَّسُ
(Better than the people who disobey their commander — O people, be ashamed! — are the women who sit at home.)
The meaning is: خيرٌ مِنَ القَوْمِ العصاةِ أميرَهُم النِّساءُ الجُلَّسُ يا قومُ فاسْتَحْيُوا. Another said [in the basīṭ metre, and it is the two hundred and ninth poetic witness]:
الشَّمْشُ طالِعَةٌ لَيْسَتْ بِكاسِفَةٍ * تَبْكِي عليكَ نُجُومَ اللَّيْلِ والقَمَرا
(The sun has risen yet does not eclipse the stars of the night and the moon, weeping for you.)
Its meaning is: the sun has risen and has not eclipsed the stars of the night and the moon, because of its grief over "ʿUmar". That is because whenever the sun rises it eclipses the moon and the stars and leaves them no light.
Among the meanings of the Qur'an is the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلاَ تَنكِحُواْ مَا نَكَحَ آبَاؤُكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ إِلاَّ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾. The meaning is not "marry what has already passed"; that is not permissible in speech. The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "Do not marry the women your fathers married, for you will be punished for it, except what has already passed, for Allah has remitted it from you." Likewise His words ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهَاتُكُمْ وَبَنَاتُكُمْ﴾, then He said ﴿وَأَن تَجْمَعُواْ بَيْنَ ٱلاخْتَيْنِ إَلاَّ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾; the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: you will be held to account for that, except what has already passed, for Allah has remitted it from you.
And His words ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِي حَآجَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي رِبِّهِ﴾, then He said ﴿أَوْ كَٱلَّذِي مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ﴾: the "kāf" is added in speech, and the meaning is: "Have you not seen the one who disputed with Ibrāhīm about his Lord, or the one who passed by a town?" Its like in the Qur'an is ﴿لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ﴾, and the meaning is "There is nothing like Him", because Allah has no like. The poet said [in the rajaz metre, and it is the two hundred and tenth poetic witness]:
* فَصُيِّرُوا مثلَ كَعَصْفٍ مَأْكُول *
(So they were made like eaten straw.)
The meaning is "they were made like straw", and the kāf is redundant (zāʾida). Another said [rajaz, and it is the two hundred and eleventh poetic witness]:
* وَصَالِباتٍ كَكَما يُؤَثْفِين *
(And firm hearth-stones, as they are set up as trivets.)
One of the two kāfs is redundant.
And His words ﴿بَدَّلْنَاهُمْ جُلُوداً غَيْرَهَا﴾ mean "other than them in being roasted", because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, renews them so that it is a severer punishment for them. They are those very same skins that disobeyed Allah the Exalted, but their being roasted is removed, just as a man says to another: "أنتَ اليومَ غيرُك أمْسِ" (Today you are other than you were yesterday), while he is the very same, except that something has decreased in him or increased. And in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلَوْ رُدُّواْ لَعَادُواْ لِمَا نُهُواْ عَنْهُ وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾. A questioner may ask: how were they liars when they had not yet returned? They would only be liars if they returned. And you have said that one is not called an unbeliever before he disbelieves, even if it is known that he will be an unbeliever. This may mean that they are the liars after this day, just as a man says "أَنَا قائِمٌ" (I am standing) while he is sitting, meaning "I shall stand". Or He says ﴿إِنَّهم لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾ meaning the lying and unbelief with which they arrived at the Resurrection, because those who entered the Fire were liars and unbelievers.
And His words ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَّاضِرَةٌ إِلىٰ رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ﴾: He says "they look to their provision and what comes to them from Allah", just as a man says: "ما أَنْظُرُ إِلاّ إِلَيك" (I look only to you). If it were the looking of the eye, as some people say, the following verse would have made that clear. Do you not see that He said ﴿وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ باسِرةٌ تَظُنُّ أَن يُفْعَلَ بِها فَاقِرَةٌ﴾ and did not say "and faces that do not look and do not see"? And His words ﴿تَظُنُّ أَن يُفْعَلَ بِهَا فَاقِرَةٌ﴾: the "supposing" here indicates that the looking there is trust in Allah and good certainty, and does not indicate what they said. How could that be, when Allah says ﴿لاَّ تُدْرِكُهُ ٱلأَبْصَارُ وَهُوَ يُدْرِكُ ٱلأَبْصَارَ﴾? [Translator's note: this is the author's own theological position on the vision of Allah, translated as written.] And His words ﴿وَمَا تَشَآءُونَ إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾ mean: you do not will anything of good unless Allah wills that you will it.
And His words ﴿إِذَآ أَخْرَجَ يَدَهُ لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاهَا﴾: this is construed according to the meaning, namely that he does not see it. For when you say "كادَ يفعل" you mean only that he came close to doing it but did not do it; and when you say "لم يكد يفعل", the meaning is that he did not come close to doing it and did not do it — this is the correct sense of the speech, and such is the meaning of this verse. However, the language has also allowed "لَمْ يَكَدْ يَفْعَلُ" in the sense of "he did it after difficulty", but this is not the correct sense of the speech, because when one says "كاد يفعل" he means only "he came close to doing it", and when he says "لم يكد يفعل" he is saying "he did not come close to doing it". However, the language has come as I have explained to you, and that is not according to the correct sense of the word.

akhfash:63-63.t: He said: ﴿أَوَ عَجِبْتُمْ أَن جَآءَكُمْ ذِكْرٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ﴾. It is as though it were said: "They did such-and-such and wondered", so He said: "You did such-and-such — and do you wonder (أَوَعَجِبْتُمْ)?" This is the wāw of conjunction, with the interrogative alif prefixed to it.

akhfash:65-65.t:
He said: ﴿وَإِلَىٰ عَادٍ أَخَاهُمْ هُوداً﴾ and ﴿وَإِلَىٰ ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمْ صَالِحاً﴾. All of this — and Allah knows best — is accusative (manṣūb) by the first statement, i.e. by His words ﴿لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحاً إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ﴾; and likewise ﴿لُوطاً﴾. Some said it means "واذْكُرْ لُوطاً" (and mention Lūṭ). This accusative comes only by one of these two ways, or by the verb having governed something before it, and then a verb falls after it on something connected with it, so a verb is implied for it. So it is only by one of these three, and this is frequent in the Qur'an.
And He said ﴿خَلاَئِفَ ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ and He said ﴿خُلَفَآءَ﴾; all are permissible, and it is the plural of "الخليفة".

akhfash:69-69.t: He said: ﴿وَزَادَكُمْ فِي ٱلْخَلْقِ بَسْطَةً﴾, i.e. "انْبِساطاً" (extension). In another place it is ﴿بَسْطَةً فِي ٱلْعِلْمِ وَٱلْجِسْمِ﴾, and it is like the first.

akhfash:73-73.t: He said: ﴿فَذَرُوهَا تَأْكُلْ فِيۤ أَرْضِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: jussive (majzūm) if you make it an apodosis (jawāb), and nominative (marfūʿ) if you mean "فَذَرُوها آكِلَةً" (leave her eating). And He said ﴿وَأْمُرْ قَوْمَكَ يَأْخُذُواْ بِأَحْسَنِهَا﴾, and He said ﴿قُل لِّلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ يَغْفِرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ﴾ and ﴿فَذَرْهُمْ يَخُوضُواْ وَيَلْعَبُواْ﴾: it has become an apodosis in wording, but it is not so in meaning.

akhfash:86-86.t: Then He said: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْعُدُواْ بِكُلِّ صِرَاطٍ تُوعِدُونَ﴾. You say "هُمْ فِي البَصْرَةِ" and "بِالبَصْرَةِ" (they are in Basra), and "قَعَدْتُ لَهُ في الطَّريق" and "بِالطَّريق" (I lay in wait for him on the road).

akhfash:92-92.t: He said: ﴿كَأَن لَّمْ يَغْنَوْاْ فِيهَا﴾; it is from "غَنِيتَ" "تَغْنَى" "غِنَى" (to dwell, abide).

akhfash:98-98.t: He said: ﴿أَوَ أَمِنَ أَهْلُ ٱلْقُرَىٰ﴾: this wāw is for conjunction, with the interrogative alif prefixed to it.

akhfash:100-100.t: He said: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لِلَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ ٱلأَرْضَ مِن بَعْدِ أَهْلِهَآ﴾; he says: "Has it not become clear to them?" Some read ﴿نَهْدِ﴾ with nūn, i.e. "Have We not made clear to them" ﴿أَن لَّوْ نَشَآءُ أَصَبْنَاهُمْ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ﴾.

akhfash:101-101.t:
He said: ﴿نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنبَآئِهَا﴾: he made "مِنْ" redundant and meant "قصَصْنا" (We have related), just as you say "هل لكَ في ذا" (Do you have [a need] for this?) and omit "حاجة" (need).
And He said ﴿فَمَا كَانُواْ لِيُؤْمِنُواْ بِمَا كَذَّبُواْ مِن قَبْلُ﴾: His words ﴿بما كذبو﴾ — and Allah knows best — mean "بِتَكْذِيبِهِم" (because of their denial). He made — and Allah knows best — ﴿مَا كَذَّبُوا﴾ a noun for the action (i.e. a maṣdar, verbal noun), and the meaning is: "they were not such as to believe because of the denial", i.e. We do not call them believers on account of the denial.

akhfash:105-105.t: He said: ﴿حَقِيقٌ عَلَى أَنْ لاَّ أَقُولَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلاَّ ٱلْحَقَّ﴾, and some read ﴿عَلَى أَنْ لا أَقُولَ﴾. [Translator's note: the two readings appear identically in the source; the variant intended is presumably «عَلَيَّ أَنْ لا أَقُولَ».] The first is the better of the two in our view; he meant: "It is incumbent upon me that I not say." The other means: "I am worthy, upon me, that I not say against Allah", and he means "بِأَنْ لا أقولَ على الله" (that I not say against Allah), just as He said ﴿بِكُلِّ صِرَاطٍ تُوعِدُونَ﴾ in the sense of "على كُلِّ صِراطٍ تُوعِدُون" (on every path, threatening).

akhfash:111-111.t: He said: ﴿أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ﴾ and He said ﴿تُرْجِي مَن تَشَآءُ مِنْهُنَّ﴾, because it is from "أَرْجأْتُ" (I postponed). It has been read ﴿أَرْجِهِ وَأَخاه﴾, lightened without hamza, and that is how we read, and ﴿تُرْجِي مَن تَشَآءُ﴾. It is a dialect in which one says "أَرْجَيْتُ"; and some Arabs say "أَخْطَيْتُ" and "تَوَضَّيْتُ", without hamza.

akhfash:126-126.t: He said: ﴿وَمَا تَنقِمُ مِنَّآ﴾, and some read ﴿وَمَا تَنْقَمُ مِنّا﴾. They are two dialects: "نَقَمَ" "يَنْقِمُ" and "نَقِم" "يَنْقَمُ". And we read with it — i.e. with the first.

akhfash:132-132.t: He said: ﴿وَقَالُواْ مَهْمَا تَأْتِنَا بِهِ مِن آيَةٍ﴾, because ﴿مَهْما﴾ is one of the particles of condition (ḥurūf al-mujāzāt), and its apodosis is ﴿فَمَا نَحْنُ﴾.

akhfash:133-133.t:
He said: ﴿ٱلطُّوفَانَ﴾; its singular by analogy (qiyās) is "الطُوفانَة". The poet said [in the ramal metre, and it is the two hundred and twelfth poetic witness]:
* غَيْرَ اَلجِدَّةَ مِنْ آياتِها خُرُقُ الرِّيحِ وَطُوفَانُ المَطَر *
(Its traces' freshness was altered by violent winds and the deluge of rain.)
It is from "طافَ" "يَطُوفُ" (to go round).

akhfash:137-137.t: He said: ﴿وَمَا كَانُواْ يَعْرِشُونَ﴾; "يَعْرُشونَ" — two dialects. Likewise ﴿نَبْطِشُ﴾ and "نَبْطُشُ", "يَحْشُرُ" and ﴿يحشِرُ﴾, ﴿يعكُفُ﴾ and ﴿يعكِفُ﴾, ﴿ينفُرُ﴾ and ﴿ينفِرُ﴾.

akhfash:143-143.t:
He said: ﴿جَعَلَهُ دَكّاً﴾, because when He said ﴿جَعَلَه﴾ it was as though He had said "دَكَّهُ" (He levelled it) [so دكّا is a maṣdar]. One also says ﴿دَكّاء﴾; if that is meant, then it has been treated like ﴿وَسْئَلِ ٱلْقَرْيَةَ﴾ [i.e. with a muḍāf omitted], because one says "نَاقَةٌ دَكّاءُ" (a she-camel whose hump has gone).
And He said ﴿فَلَمَّا تَجَلَّىٰ رَبُّهُ لِلْجَبَلِ﴾; he says: "His command appeared", like what people say: "بَرَزَ فُلانٌ لفُلانٍ" (So-and-so came out against so-and-so), when it was only his army that came out.
As for His words ﴿رَبِّ أَرِنِيۤ أَنظُرْ إِلَيْكَ﴾, he meant only a knowledge whose like is attained only in the Hereafter, so Allah informed Mūsā that this does not happen in this world. Some read it ﴿دَكّاء﴾, making it of the pattern "فَعْلاء"; this does not seem likely. In the speech of the Arabs it is "ناقَةٌ دَكّاءُ", i.e. having no hump. And "الجبل" (the mountain) is masculine, unless it is "جَعَلَهُ مِثْلَ دَكّاءَ" (He made it like a humpless one) with "مِثْل" omitted.

akhfash:148-148.t:
He said: ﴿مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ﴾, and some read ﴿حِلِيِّهِم﴾ and ﴿حَلْيِهِم﴾; ﴿عِجْلاً جَسَداً لَّهُ خُوَارٌ﴾, and some read ﴿جُوْارٌ﴾; and all are among the dialects of the Arabs.
As for His words ﴿مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ﴾ with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, it is "فُعول", the plural of "الحَلْيِ"; and whoever says ﴿حِلِيِّهِم﴾ in the other dialect does so on account of the yāʾ, just as they said "قِسِيّ" (bows) and "عِصِيّ" (sticks).

akhfash:149-149.t: He said: ﴿وَلَمَّا سُقِطَ فَيۤ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾, and some read ﴿سَقَطَ﴾; all are permissible. The Arabs say "سُقِطَ في يديه" (he was filled with regret) and ﴿أُسْقِطَ في أيْدِيهِم﴾.

akhfash:150-150.t:
He said: ﴿ٱبْنَ أُمَّ إِنَّ ٱلْقَوْمَ﴾. That is — and Allah knows best — because he made it a single noun, like their saying "ابْنَ عَمِّ أَقْبِلْ" (Son of my uncle, come here!); this is not to be used as a basis for analogy. Some read ﴿يا ابنَ أُمي لا تَأْخُذ﴾, which is the analogical form, but the written text (al-kitāb, the muṣḥaf) has no yāʾ in it, so that was disliked. The poet said [in the khafīf metre, and it is the two hundred and thirteenth poetic witness]:
يَا ابْنَ أُميّ وَلَوْ شَهِدْتُكَ إِذْ تَدْ * عَو تَمِيماً وَأَنْتَ غَيْرَ مُجابِ
(O son of my mother, if only I had witnessed you when you called on Tamīm and were not answered.)
Some read ﴿ياابْنَ أُمِّ﴾, making it follow the dialect of those who say "this is my boy who has come" [i.e. dropping the possessive yāʾ and keeping the kasra], "or he made it a single noun whose end is kasra-marked", like "خازِبازِ".
And He said ﴿وَكَادُواْ يَقْتُلُونَنِي﴾: two nūns are retained in it, one belonging to the verb and the other to the latent (implied) pronoun noun. [Translator's note: the second nūn is in fact the nūn al-wiqāya before the attached pronoun ي; the source says «للاسم المضمر».] It is retained in the verb only because it is nominative, and the nominative of the verb, when it is for the plural or the dual, is by retaining the nūn; except that the plural nūn has fatḥa and the dual nūn has kasra. He has said ﴿أَتَعِدَانِنِيۤ أَنْ أُخْرَجَ﴾. Assimilation (idghām) and concealment (ikhfāʾ) are also permissible in this.

akhfash:154-154.t:
He said: ﴿وَلَماَّ سَكَتَ عَن مُّوسَى ٱلْغَضَبُ﴾, and some read ﴿سَكَنَ﴾, except that it does not accord with the written text, so ﴿سَكَتَ﴾ is read; and both are of the speech of the Arabs.
And He said ﴿لِّلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ﴾, just as He said ﴿إِن كُنتُمْ لِلرُّؤْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ﴾: He joined the verb [to its object] with the lām. Some said it means ﴿مِنْ أَجْلِ رَبِّهِم يَرْهَبُون﴾ (they fear for the sake of their Lord).

akhfash:155-155.t:
He said: ﴿وَٱخْتَارَ مُوسَىٰ قَوْمَهُ سَبْعِينَ رَجُلاً﴾, i.e. "he chose from his people"; when "مِنْ" was removed, the verb governed [the noun directly]. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre, and it is the fourteenth poetic witness]: [Translator's note: the numbering here (14th, 15th, 16th) is as written in the source, which elsewhere in this passage counts above two hundred.]
مِنا الذي اخْتِيرَ الرجال سَماحَةً * وَجْوداً إِذا هَبَّ الرِّياحُ الزَعازِعُ
(From us is the one chosen from among men for magnanimity and generosity when the violent winds blow.)
Another said [in the basīṭ metre, and it is the fifteenth poetic witness]:
أَمَرْتُكَ الخَيْرَ فافْعَلْ ما أُمِرْتَ بِهِ * فَقَدْ تَرَكْتُكَ ذا مالٍ وَذا نَشَبِ
(I commanded you [to do] good, so do what you were commanded, for I have left you possessed of wealth and property.)
And al-Nābigha said [in the kāmil metre, and it is the sixteenth poetic witness]:
نُبِّئْتُ زُرْعةَ وَالسفَاهَةُ كاسْمِها * يُهْدِي إِلَيَّ أَوَابِدَ الأشْعار
(I was told [about] Zurʿa — and folly is as its name — that he sends me wild, unruly verses.)

akhfash:156-156.t: He said: ﴿وَرَحْمَتِي وَسِعَتْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾, i.e. it encompasses everyone who enters into it and does not fall short of anyone who enters it; or it may mean the mercy that He has divided among the creatures, by which some of them show tenderness to others, even the tenderness of the beast towards its young.

akhfash:160-160.t: He said: ﴿ٱثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ أَسْبَاطاً﴾: He meant twelve groups, then informed that the groups are tribes (asbāṭ); He did not make the number apply to "the tribes" [as its tamyīz, specification].

akhfash:168-168.t: He said: ﴿مِّنْهُمُ ٱلصَّالِحُونَ وَمِنْهُمْ دُونَ ذٰلِكَ﴾; we know of no one who reads it other than with the accusative.

akhfash:169-169.t:
He said: ﴿فَخَلَفَ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌ﴾. When you say "خَلَفُ سَوءٍ" (an evil successor) and "خَلَفُ صِدْقٍ" (a true successor), the two are the same. By "الخَلْفُ" one means only what comes after what has passed, whether it was a successor (khalaf) from it or not; what is meant by it is the generation that comes after a generation. And "الخَلَفُ" is that which is a replacement for what was before it, having taken its place and done its work. You say: "أَصَبْتُ مِنْكَ خَلَفا" (I have found in you a replacement).
And He said ﴿يَأْخُذُونَ عَرَضَ هَـٰذَا ٱلأَدْنَىٰ﴾: He annexed "العَرَضَ" to "هذا" and explained "هذا" by "الأَدْنى". Everything is ʿarḍ (goods) except dirhams and dinars, which are ʿayn (cash); whatever is other than that is ʿarḍ. As for "العَرَضُ", it is everything that befalls you. You say: "قد عرض له بعدي عَرُضٌ", i.e. "a calamity and evil befell him after me". And you say: "هذا عُرْضَةٌ للشَرِّ" (this is exposed to evil) and "عُرْضَةٌ للخَيْر" (exposed to good); all this the Arabs say. He said ﴿وَلاَ تَجْعَلُواْ ٱللَّهَ عُرْضَةً لأَيْمَانِكُمْ﴾. And you say "أَعْرَضَ لكَ الخيرُ" and "عَرَضَ لكَ الخَيْرُ" (good presented itself to you). The poet said [in the kāmil metre, and it is the two hundred and seventeenth poetic witness]: [Translator's note: the previous witness in this passage was numbered the sixteenth; the numbering is as in the source.]
أَعْرِفَنَّكَ مُعْرِضاً لِرِماحِنَا * في جُفِّ تُغْلِبَ واردَ الأَمْرارِ
(Let me not find you exposing yourself to our spears among the throng of Taghlib, coming down to the bitter waters.)
And "العارِضُ" of clouds is what faces you; it is the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عَارِضاً﴾. As for "الحَبِيُّ", it is what comes from every direction. You say "خُذُوهْ من عُرْضِ الناس", i.e. from those of them nearest you; likewise "اضرب به عُرْضَ الحائط", i.e. the part of it nearest you. As for "العَرْضُ" (breadth) as against "الطول" (length), it is with sukūn. As for his words [in the ṭawīl metre, and it is the two hundred and eighteenth poetic witness]:
[لَهُنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ عادَةٌ قَدْ عَرَفْنَها] * إِذا عَرَضُوا الخَطِّيَّ فَوْقَ الكَوَاثِب
(They [the horses] have a habit with them that they know well: when they lay the Khaṭṭī spears crosswise over the withers.)
and "أعرضوا" — this is because of: عَرَضَ عَرْضاً. And "عَرَضْتُ عَلَيْهِ المَنْزِلَ عَرْضاً" (I offered him the dwelling) and "عَرَضَ لِيَ أَمْرٌ عَرْضاً" (a matter presented itself to me): this is its maṣdar. And "العَرَضُ من الخَيْرِ والشَرِّ": whatever ʿaraḍ of this world you obtain and benefit from, by which you mean good. And "عَرَضَ لك عَرَضُ سَوْءٍ" (an evil accident befell you).

akhfash:176-176.t: He said: ﴿وَلَـٰكِنَّهُ أَخْلَدَ إِلَى ٱلأَرْضِ﴾; we know of no one who says ﴿خَلَدَ﴾. His words ﴿أَخْلَدَ﴾ mean: he resorted to it.

akhfash:177-177.t: He said: ﴿سَآءَ مَثَلاً ٱلْقَوْمُ﴾: in wording He made "القومُ" (the people) the "المَثَل" (the likeness), but He meant "the likeness of the people", and omitted it, just as He said "وَاسْأَل القَرْيَةَ".

akhfash:179-179.t: He said: ﴿وَلَقَدْ ذَرَأْنَا لِجَهَنَّمَ﴾; you say "ذَرَأَ" "يَذْرأُ" "ذَرْءاً" (to create, multiply).

akhfash:180-180.t: He said: ﴿وَذَرُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ يُلْحِدُونَ فِيۤ أَسْمَآئِهِ﴾, and some read ﴿يُلْحَدُونَ﴾, deriving it from "لَحَدَ" "يَلْحَدُ", which is a dialect. [Translator's note: the variant is printed as «يُلْحَدُونَ» in the source; from لَحَدَ يَلْحَدُ one would expect «يَلْحَدُونَ».] And He said in another place ﴿لِّسَانُ ٱلَّذِي يُلْحِدُونَ﴾ and ﴿يَلْحَدُون﴾; they are two dialects, and ﴿يُلْحدُونَ﴾ is more frequent, and that is how we read; it is supported by ﴿وَمَن يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحَادٍ بِظُلْمٍ﴾.

akhfash:189-189.t: He said: ﴿حَمَلَتْ حَمْلاً خَفِيفاً﴾, because "الحَمْلَ" is what is in the belly and "الحِمْل" is what is on the back. And He said ﴿وَتَضَعُ كُلُّ ذَاتِ حَمْلٍ حَمْلَهَا﴾. As for His words ﴿أَثْقَلَتْ﴾, he says: "she became heavy-laden", just as you say "أَتْمَرْنا", i.e. "we came to have dates", and "أَلْبَنَّا" [i.e. we came to have milk], and "أَعْشَبَتِ الأَرْضُ" (the land became grassy) and "أَكْمَأَتْ" (it produced truffles). Some read ﴿فَلَمّا أُثْقِلَتْ﴾.

akhfash:190-190.t: He said: ﴿جَعَلاَ لَهُ شُرَكَآءَ فِيمَآ آتَاهُمَا﴾, and some read ﴿شِرْكاً﴾, because "الشِرْكَ" is just "الشِرْكَةُ" (partnership); and according to whoever reads thus, it ought to have said "فَجَعلا لغيرِه شِرْكاً فيما آتاهما" (so they gave others than Him a share in what He gave them).

akhfash:201-201.t:
He said: ﴿إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ طَائِفٌ مِّنَ ٱلشَّيْطَانِ﴾, and ﴿الطَيْفُ﴾ is more frequent in the speech of the Arabs. The poet said [in the mutaqārib metre, and it is the two hundred and nineteenth poetic witness]:
أَلا يَا لَقَوْمٍ لِطَيْفِ الخَيالِ * أَرَّقَ مِنْ نازِحٍ ذِي دَلالِ
(O people, behold the phantom of the dream-image that kept me awake, from a coy one far away!)
We read it ﴿طائِف﴾ because the generality of the Readers follow it.

akhfash:205-205.t: He said: ﴿بِٱلْغُدُوِّ وَٱلآصَالِ﴾; its explanation is "بالغَدَواَتِ" (in the mornings), just as you say "آتيك طلوعَ الشَمْسِ" (I will come to you at sunrise), i.e. at the time of sunrise, as He said ﴿بِٱلْعَشِيِّ وَٱلإِبْكَارِ﴾. It is like "آتيكَ في الصَّباحِ وبِالمَساءِ" (I will come to you in the morning and in the evening). As for ﴿الآصال﴾, its singular is "أَصيلٌ", like "الأَشْرار" whose singular is "الشَرِير", and "الأَيْمانُ" whose singular is "اليَمِينُ".

akhfash:2-2.t:
[He said] ﴿كِتَابٌ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ﴾ as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
And He said ﴿فَلاَ يَكُنْ فِي صَدْرِكَ حَرَجٌ مِّنْهُ﴾ as a prohibition, as He said ﴿وَلاَ تَعْدُ عَيْنَاكَ عَنْهُمْ﴾, i.e. "as for distress, let it not be in your breast", and "as for your eyes, let them not pass beyond them".

akhfash:6-6.t: And He said ﴿فَلَنَسْأَلَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾, meaning: [We shall surely ask] the people to whom [messengers] were sent and who were warned. ﴿وَلَنَسْأَلَنَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾.

akhfash:7-7.t: ﴿فَلَنَقُصَّنَّ﴾: He put in the nūn and the lām because His saying ﴿فَلَنَسْأَلَنَّ﴾ ﴿وَلَنَسْأَلَنَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾ is [in the form of] an oath.

akhfash:10-10.t: And He said ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا لَكُمْ فِيهَا مَعَايِشَ﴾: the yāʾ is without hamza. Some readers have pronounced it with hamza, and that is poor, because it is not additional [i.e. it is radical]. Only what is on the pattern "مَفاعِل" is pronounced with hamza when the yāʾ is additional in the singular, as are the alif and the wāw [in the singular] whose place the hamza takes, as in "مَدائِن" (cities), because it is "فَعايِل". Whoever takes "المدائِن" from "دان", "يَدِين" does not use hamza, because the yāʾ is then radical. As for "قَطائِع", "رسائِل", "عَجائزِ" and "كبائر", all of these have hamza, because the wāw of "عَجُوز" is additional — do you not see that you say "عجزَ"? — and the alif of "رسالة" is additional, [since] you say "أَرسلت" and its alif goes; and you say of "كبيرة": "كبرت", and its yāʾ goes. As for "مصايِب" (misfortunes), its origin was "مصاوب", because when the yāʾ's origin is wāw and it comes in a position where it must be vowelled, the wāw is changed in that position [into yāʾ] if the origin is from wāw; and when it was changed, it became as if it had been corrupted, until it became as if it were the additional yāʾ; therefore it was given hamza, though analogy did not require that it take hamza. And some people among the Arabs say "المصاوب", and that is the regular analogy.

akhfash:11-11.t: And He said ﴿ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَاكُمْ ثُمَّ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلاۤئِكَةِ﴾, because "ثُمَّ" has the meaning of wāw. And it may be that its meaning is [We fashioned] ﴿لآدَم﴾ (Adam), as you say to a people "قَدْ ضَرَبْناكُم" (we have struck you) when you struck only their chief.

akhfash:12-12.t:
And He said ﴿مَا مَنَعَكَ أَلاَّ تَسْجُدَ﴾; its meaning is: what prevented you from prostrating; and ﴿لا﴾ here is zāʾida (redundant). The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the two hundred and fourth shāhid]:
أَبى جُودُهُ "لا" البُخْل واستعجلتْ بِهِ * "نَعَمْ" مِنْ فَتىً لا يَمْنَع الجوعِ قاتلَه
(His generosity refused the "no" of stinginess, and "yes" hastened [to come] from a young man who does not withhold from hunger its killer [i.e. food].)
The Arabs explained it: his generosity refused stinginess*, and they made ﴿لا﴾ redundant here as padding, connecting the speech with it. Yūnus claimed that Abū ʿAmr used to put "البخل" in the genitive and not make "لا" a construct attached to it [Translator's note: as written; the sense rather requires that he made "لا" the first term of a construct with "البخل"]; he meant: his generosity refused the ﴿لا﴾ which is for stinginess, because ﴿لا﴾ may be [a word] of generosity or of stinginess: if someone said to him "withhold the due" or "do not give the poor", and he said "no", this would be generosity from him.

akhfash:16-16.t:
And He said ﴿لأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَاطَكَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ﴾, i.e. on (على) Your path; and as you say "تَوَجَّهَ مَكَّةَ" (he headed Mecca), i.e. to Mecca. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the two hundred and fifth shāhid]:
كَأَنِّيَ إِذْ أَسْعَى لأَظْفَرَ طائراً * معَ النَّجْم في جَوِّ السَّماءِ يَصُوبُ
(It is as though, when I strive to catch [her], [I strive for] a bird swooping with the star in the vault of the sky.)
He means: to catch a bird (بطائرٍ); he dropped the bāʾ. And like it is ﴿أَعَجِلْتُمْ أَمْرَ رَبِّكُمْ﴾, meaning: [hastened] away from (عن) the command of your Lord.

akhfash:18-18.t:
And He said ﴿ٱخْرُجْ مِنْهَا مَذْءُوماً مَّدْحُوراً ﴾, because it is from "الذَأم" (disgrace): you say "ذَأَمْتُه", so "هُوَ مَذْؤُومٌ". The other way is from "الذَمّ" (blame): "ذَمَمْتُه", so "هو مَذْمُومٌ". You say "ذَأَمْتُهُ", "ذَمَمْتُه" and "ذِمْتُه", all in one meaning; and the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "ذِمْتُهُ" is "الذَّيْم".
And He said ﴿وَلَّمَن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ لأَمْلأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ﴾: the first lām is the lām of ibtidāʾ (inception) and the second is for the oath.

akhfash:20-20.t:
And He said ﴿فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَانُ﴾, and the meaning is: Satan whispered to (إلى) them. But the Arabs connect the verb with all these particles. Some of them say "غَرِضْتُ" in the sense of "I longed for him", and its explanation is: I grew weary of these [and turned] to him.
And He said ﴿إِلاَّ أَنْ تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ﴾, meaning: ﴿ما نَهاكُما إلاّ﴾ out of dislike ﴿أَن تَكُونَا﴾, as you say "إِيَاكَ أَنْ تَفْعَلَ" (beware of doing), i.e. out of dislike that you should do.

akhfash:22-22.t:
And He said ﴿وَطَفِقَا﴾, and some read ﴿وَطَفقَا﴾. Whoever says "طَفَقَ" says "يَطْفِقُ", and whoever says "طَفِقَ" says "يَطْفَقُ".
And He said ﴿يَخْصِفَانِ﴾: he takes it from "يَخْتَصِفانِ"; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṣād and became unvowelled, and the khāʾ remained unvowelled, so the khāʾ was given kasra because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters. Some of them give the khāʾ fatḥa, transferring the vowel of the tāʾ to it. It is like His saying ﴿أَمَّن لاَّ يَهِدِّيۤ﴾; and some read ﴿يَهِدِّي الا ان يُهْدَى﴾.

akhfash:23-23.t: And He said ﴿وَإِن لَّمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْخَاسِرِينَ﴾: it is as though it is an oath — and Allah knows best — as if they said: "By Allah, we shall surely be among the losers if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us".

akhfash:26-26.t: And He said ﴿قَدْ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ لِبَاساً يُوَارِي سَوْءَاتِكُمْ وَرِيشاً وَلِبَاسُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ ذٰلِكَ خَيْرٌ﴾: He put His saying ﴿وَلِبَاسُ ٱلتَّقْوىٰ﴾ in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and placed its khabar (predicate) in His saying ﴿ذٰلِكَ خَيْرٌ﴾. Some put ﴿وَلِباسَ التّقْوى﴾ in the accusative. And some read ﴿وَرِيشاً﴾, and that is how we read it; both are good and their meaning is one. [Translator's note: the other reading was evidently «وَرِيَاشاً»; the text writes ﴿وَرِيشاً﴾ both times.]

akhfash:30-30.t: And He said ﴿وَفَرِيقاً حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلضَّلاَلَةُ﴾, making the verb masculine because of the separation [between it and its feminine subject], as He said ﴿لاَ يُؤْخَذُ مِنكُمْ فِدْيَةٌ﴾.

akhfash:35-35.t: And He said ﴿يَابَنِيۤ آدَمَ إِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِّنكُمْ يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آيَاتِي فَمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰ وَأَصْلَحَ فَلاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: it was as if He said "then obey them".

akhfash:40-40.t: And He said ﴿حَتَّىٰ يَلِجَ ٱلْجَمَلُ فِي سَمِّ ٱلْخِيَاطِ﴾, from "وَلَجَ", "يَلِجُ", "وُلُوجاً" (to enter).

akhfash:41-41.t: And He said ﴿لَهُمْ مِّن جَهَنَّمَ مِهَادٌ وَمِن فَوْقِهِمْ غَوَاشٍ﴾. His saying (غَواشٍ) has kasra only because this shīn is in the position of the ʿayn of "فواعِل", so it has kasra. As for the position of its lām [final radical], it is the yāʾ; and the yāʾ and the wāw, when they come after a kasra in a position to be vowelled with nominative or genitive, become an unvowelled yāʾ in the nominative and genitive, and take fatḥa in the accusative. When they became an unvowelled yāʾ and the tanwīn, which is unvowelled, was added to it, the yāʾ went because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters.

akhfash:43-44.t:
And He said ﴿وَنَزَعْنَا مَا فِي صُدُورِهِم مِّنْ غِلٍّ﴾: it is what is in the breasts [i.e. rancour]; as for that with which the captive is fettered, it is "الغُلّ" (the shackle).
And He said ﴿ٱلْحَمْدُ للَّهِ ٱلَّذِي هَدَانَا لِهَـٰذَا﴾, as He said ﴿ٱللَّهُ يَهْدِي لِلْحَقِّ﴾. The Arabs say "هوَ لا يَهتَدِي لهذا", i.e. he does not know it. You say "هَدَيْتُ العروسَ إِلى بَعْلِها" (I led the bride to her husband), and you also say "أَهْدَيْتُها إلَيْه" and "هُدِيَتْ لَهُ", and you say "أَهْدَيْتُ لَهُ هَدِيَّةً" (I gave him a gift). The Banū Tamīm say "هَدَيْت العروسَ إِلى زَوْجِها", taking it in the sense of "I guided her", and Qays say "أَهْدَيْتُها", treating her like a gift.
And He said ﴿وَنُودُوۤاْ أَن تِلْكُمُ ٱلْجَنَّةُ﴾ and ﴿أَن لَّعْنَةُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَى ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾, and He said in another place ﴿أَنِ ٱلْحَمْدُ للَّهِ﴾ and ﴿أَن قَدْ وَجَدْنَا مَا وَعَدَنَا رَبُّنَا حَقّاً﴾. This is the heavy "أَنّ" lightened, with [the pronoun] implied in it; it is not right to take it as the light [أَنْ], because after it is a noun, and nouns do not follow the light one. The poet said [in the basīṭ metre; this is the two hundred and sixth shāhid]:
فِيَ فِتْيَةٍ كَسُيوفِ الهِنْدِ قَدْ عَلِمُوا * أنْ هالِكٌ كُلُّ مَنْ يَخْفى وَينْتَعِل
(Among young men like Indian swords, who know that everyone who goes barefoot or shod is perishing.) [Translator's note: «يَخْفى» is evidently for «يَحْفى» "goes barefoot".]
And the poet said [in the wāfir metre; this is the two hundred and seventh shāhid]:
أُكاشِرُهُ وَاَعْلَمُ أَنْ كِلانا * عَلَى ما سَاءَ صاحِبَهُ حَريصُ
(I grin at him, knowing that each of us is eager for what harms the other.)
Its meaning is: that (أَنْهُ) each of us. And ﴿أَن قَدْ وَجَدْنَا﴾ may be in the sense of "أي" (that is to say).

akhfash:50-50.t: And His saying ﴿أَنْ أَفِيضُواْ عَلَيْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ﴾ may be "أيْ أَفِيضوا" (that is: pour), or it may be the "أنْ" that governs verbs, because you say "غَاظَني أَنْ قامَ" (it angered me that he stood) and "غَاظَنِي أَنْ ذَهَب" (it angered me that he went), so it falls on [past] verbs even though it does not govern them. In the Book of Allah: ﴿وَٱنطَلَقَ ٱلْمَلأُ مِنْهُمْ أَنِ ٱمْشُواْ﴾, whose meaning is: that is, walk on.

akhfash:53-53.t: And He said ﴿فَهَل لَّنَا مِن شُفَعَآءَ فَيَشْفَعُواْ لَنَآ أَوْ نُرَدُّ فَنَعْمَلَ غَيْرَ ٱلَّذِي كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ﴾: He put what follows the fāʾ in the accusative because it is the answer to a question.

daas-irab:37-37.t: ﴿فَمَنْ﴾: مَن is an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); the fāʾ is resumptive. ﴿أَظْلَمُ﴾: its khabar (predicate). ﴿مِمَّنِ﴾: [مَن] is a relative noun, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the genitive (majrūr) by مِن; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) أظلم. ﴿افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; كذبا is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The clause ﴿أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِآياتِهِ﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَنالُهُمْ نَصِيبُهُمْ مِنَ الْكِتابِ﴾: an imperfect verb, its object and its fāʿil (agent); من الكتاب is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from نصيبهم. The verbal clause is the khabar of أولئك. ﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of limit and of the genitive. ﴿إِذا جاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُنا﴾: a past verb, its object and its agent; the tāʾ is for the feminine, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa (annexation). ﴿يَتَوَفَّوْنَهُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, its agent and its object; the clause is in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as ḥāl. The clause ﴿قالُوا﴾ has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive conditional. ﴿أَيْنَ﴾: an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿ما كُنْتُمْ﴾: ما is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ; كنتم: kāna, and the tāʾ is its noun, and the clause ﴿تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ is its khabar. ﴿قالُوا﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿ضَلُّوا عَنَّا﴾ is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl); the clause ﴿شَهِدُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ is conjoined. ﴿أَنَّهُمْ﴾: anna and its noun, and the clause ﴿كانُوا كافِرِينَ﴾ is its khabar. Anna and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive by a preposition — "they testified against themselves to their disbelief" — and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to شهدوا.

daas-irab:38-38.t:
﴿قالَ﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿ادْخُلُوا﴾: an imperative verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿فِي أُمَمٍ﴾ are attached; it is indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿قَدْ خَلَتْ﴾: قد is a particle of realization, and [خلت] is a past verb to which the following preposition and its genitive noun are attached; it is indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the tāʾ is for the feminine, and the clause is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) as an adjective (ṣifa) of أمم. ﴿مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of أمم. ﴿فِي النَّارِ﴾: attached to the verb ادخلوا. ﴿كُلَّما﴾: temporal adverbial, conveying the sense of a condition; the clause ﴿دَخَلَتْ أُمَّةٌ﴾ is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa (annexation), and the clause ﴿لَعَنَتْ أُخْتَها﴾ has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive conditional. ﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of limit and of the genitive. ﴿إِذَا﴾: a non-jussive conditional adverb.
﴿ادَّارَكُوا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is its agent. ﴿فِيها﴾: attached to اداركوا. ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa. ﴿قالَتْ﴾: a past verb. ﴿أُخْراهُمْ﴾: agent, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied on the alif because of impossibility (taʿadhdhur); هم is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa. ﴿لِأُولاهُمْ﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra implied on the alif because of impossibility; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb قالت. The clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
﴿رَبَّنا﴾: the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative (manṣūb); نا is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa. ﴿هؤُلاءِ﴾: a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), indeclinable on the kasra. ﴿أَضَلُّونا﴾: a past verb, its agent and its object, and the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿فَآتِهِمْ﴾: a verb of supplication, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, since it is weak-final; the hāʾ is its first object and the mīm is for the plural. The fāʾ before it is the faṣīḥa. ﴿عَذاباً﴾: its second object. ﴿ضِعْفاً﴾: an adjective of عذاب. ﴿مِنَ النَّارِ﴾: attached to an omitted second adjective of عذاب; the clause ﴿آتهم﴾ has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied condition. ﴿قالَ﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿لِكُلٍّ﴾: attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ ﴿ضِعْفٌ﴾, and the clause is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of قال. ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾: a particle of rectification (istidrāk), and the wāw is circumstantial.
The clause ﴿لا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl.

daas-irab:39-39.t: ﴿وَقالَتْ أُولاهُمْ لِأُخْراهُمْ﴾: its i'rab has preceded in the previous verse. ﴿فَما﴾: the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); ما is negative. ﴿كانَ﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿لَكُمْ عَلَيْنا﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of kāna. ﴿مِنْ فَضْلٍ﴾: مِن is a redundant preposition; فضل is genitive in form and nominative in position as the noun of kāna; the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl), a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَذُوقُوا﴾: the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, and the verbal clause ﴿ذوقوا الْعَذابَ﴾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position: "if the saying has taken place, then taste the punishment ...". ﴿بِما﴾: ما is relative or maṣdarī. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾: the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the clause ﴿تَكْسِبُونَ﴾ is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of كنتم.

daas-irab:40-40.t:
﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا﴾: الذين is a relative noun, the noun of inna, and the clause after it is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿اسْتَكْبَرُوا عَنْها﴾ is conjoined to it. ﴿لا تُفَتَّحُ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, and ﴿أَبْوابُ﴾ is its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿وَلا يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ﴾: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; لا is negative, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿حَتَّى يَلِجَ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) an after ḥattā; the interpreted maṣdar formed from the verb and the maṣdarī particle before it is in the position of the genitive by the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يدخلون. ﴿الْجَمَلُ﴾: agent. ﴿فِي سَمِّ﴾: attached to the verb يلج. ﴿الْخِياطِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَكَذلِكَ﴾: the demonstrative is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar: ﴿نَجْزِي الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ "a recompense like the recompense of those who denied ...".
﴿الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:41-41.t: ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿مِهادٌ﴾. ﴿مِنْ جَهَنَّمَ﴾: attached to an omitted second khabar. The nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), or resumptive with no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ﴾: attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿غَواشٍ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative with the ḍamma implied on the dropped yāʾ. ﴿وَكَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ﴾: its i'rab has preceded in the previous verse. The clause ﴿وَمِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ﴾ is conjoined.

daas-irab:42-42.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾: the clause is conjoined. ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of عملوا, accusative with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural; the verbal clause is conjoined. ﴿لا نُكَلِّفُ﴾: an imperfect verb, and لا is negative. ﴿نَفْساً﴾: first object. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿وُسْعَها﴾: second object; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "we" (نحن), and the clause is parenthetical. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَصْحابُ﴾: khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is the khabar of الذي [Translator's note: so in the source; the relative noun in the verse is الذين]. ﴿الْجَنَّةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿هُمْ﴾: a detached nominative pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِيها﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar. ﴿خالِدُونَ﴾: its khabar, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:43-43.t:
﴿وَنَزَعْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فِي صُدُورِهِمْ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿مِنْ غِلٍّ﴾: attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). The clause is conjoined. ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمُ الْأَنْهارُ﴾: an imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and الأنهار is its agent; the clause is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl. ﴿وَقالُوا﴾: the clause is conjoined. ﴿الْحَمْدُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾: attached to its omitted khabar (predicate), and the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a relative noun in the position of the genitive as an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿هَدانا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied on the alif because of impossibility (taʿadhdhur); its agent is "he" and نا is its object. ﴿لِهذا﴾: attached to هدانا. ﴿وَما﴾: ما is negative and the wāw is resumptive. ﴿كُنَّا﴾: kāna, and نا is its noun. ﴿لِنَهْتَدِيَ﴾: the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); نهتدي is accusative by an implied an after the lām of denial; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb after it is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar: "and we were not ones made able to be guided"; the clause is resumptive.
﴿لَوْلا﴾: a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿أَنْ﴾: a maṣdarī particle governing the accusative. ﴿هَدانَا اللَّهُ﴾: a past verb, its object, and the name of Majesty is its agent; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is omitted after lawlā: "were it not that Allah's guidance exists ...". ﴿لَقَدْ﴾: the lām occurs in the response to an oath; قد is a particle of realization. ﴿جاءَتْ رُسُلُ رَبِّنا﴾: a past verb, its agent and a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾: attached to an omitted ḥāl, and the clause has no grammatical position, being the response to an implied oath.
﴿وَنُودُوا﴾: a passive past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿أَنْ﴾: explicative, or lightened from anna.
﴿تِلْكُمُ﴾: a demonstrative, indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; the lām is for distance, the kāf is a particle of address, and the mīm is for the plural. ﴿الْجَنَّةُ﴾: badal (substitute) or khabar, and the clause ﴿أُورِثْتُمُوها﴾ is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl; if الجنة is parsed as badal, then the clause أورثتموها is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿أُورِثْتُمُوها﴾: a passive past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn because it is attached to the tāʾ of the agent; the tāʾ is the deputy agent, the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural, the wāw is for the lengthening of the ḍamma, and ها is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بِما﴾: ما is relative, and [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to the verb. ﴿كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾: kāna, the tāʾ is its noun, and the clause is its khabar.

daas-irab:44-44.t: ﴿وَنادى أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ أَصْحابَ النَّارِ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the implied fatḥa, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنْ قَدْ وَجَدْنا ما وَعَدَنا﴾: أن is explicative, or lightened, its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause after it is the khabar (predicate); the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb نادى: "they called out with [the announcement of] finding what was promised ...". Taking it as explicative, the clause after it is explicative with no grammatical position. ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause وعدنا is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. ﴿رَبُّنا﴾: agent. ﴿حَقًّا﴾: second object. ﴿فَهَلْ﴾: هل is an interrogative particle and the fāʾ is resumptive; the clause ﴿وَجَدْتُمْ﴾ is resumptive. ﴿قالُوا﴾: a past verb and its agent. ﴿نَعَمْ﴾: a particle of answer, and the clause ﴿فَأَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ﴾ is resumptive after the fāʾ. ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾: an adverb of time [Translator's note: so in the source; بين is usually classed as an adverb of place] attached to أذن. ﴿أَنْ﴾: lightened or explicative. ﴿لَعْنَةُ﴾: the khabar of the lightened an, or a mubtadaʾ (subject) after the explicative an. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عَلَى الظَّالِمِينَ﴾: attached to an omitted khabar. The nominal clause is explicative, or the interpreted maṣdar formed from the lightened an and the verb is in the position of the genitive. The second an is like the first, and the clause is its khabar.

daas-irab:45-45.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥ, in the position of the genitive as an adjective (ṣifa) of الظالمين. ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb يصد. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the clause ﴿يَصُدُّونَ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَيَبْغُونَها﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent) and ها its object. ﴿عِوَجاً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾: a detached nominative pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the wāw is circumstantial. ﴿بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾: attached to the khabar (predicate) after them, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl. ﴿كافِرُونَ﴾: khabar.

daas-irab:46-46.t: ﴿وَبَيْنَهُما﴾: mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); the hāʾ is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa (annexation), ما is for the dual, and the wāw is resumptive. ﴿حِجابٌ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَعَلَى الْأَعْرافِ﴾: attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ ﴿رِجالٌ﴾, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَعْرِفُونَ كُلًّا﴾: an imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿بِسِيماهُمْ﴾ are attached; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent) and كلا its object; the clause is in the position of the nominative as an adjective (ṣifa) of رجال. ﴿وَنادَوْا أَصْحابَ﴾: a past verb, its agent and its object; the clause is resumptive after the wāw. ﴿الْجَنَّةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَنْ﴾: lightened or explicative, like an in the previous verses. ﴿سَلامٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: attached to its omitted khabar, and the clause is explicative or predicative. ﴿لَمْ﴾: jussive. ﴿يَدْخُلُوها﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the agent and ها the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾: a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the clause ﴿يَطْمَعُونَ﴾ is the khabar; the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) after the circumstantial wāw.

daas-irab:47-47.t:
﴿وَإِذا﴾: إذا is an adverb that contains the sense of a condition. ﴿صُرِفَتْ أَبْصارُهُمْ﴾: a passive past verb and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿تِلْقاءَ﴾: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) صرفت. ﴿أَصْحابِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿النَّارِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa (annexation) after the conditional idhā. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾: the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative with the fatḥa; نا is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa. ﴿لا تَجْعَلْنا﴾: an imperfect verb of supplication, jussive (majzūm); نا is an attached pronoun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and لا is the prohibitive lā governing the jussive. ﴿مَعَ الْقَوْمِ﴾: attached to تجعلنا. ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa), genitive with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is a mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:48-48.t: ﴿وَنادى أَصْحابُ﴾: a past verb and fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْأَعْرافِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿رِجالًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَعْرِفُونَهُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, its agent and its object; the mīm is for the masculine plural, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿بِسِيماهُمْ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿قالُوا﴾: the clause is explicative. ﴿ما أَغْنى عَنْكُمْ جَمْعُكُمْ﴾: a past verb to which the following preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and جمعكم is its agent; ما is negative, with no governing effect, and the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun; ما is maṣdarī, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from it and the verb after it is conjoined to جمعكم: "neither your gathering nor your arrogance availed you". The clause تستكبرون is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of كنتم.

daas-irab:49-49.t:
﴿أَهؤُلاءِ﴾: a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the hāʾ is for drawing attention (tanbīh) and the hamza is interrogative.
﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable on the fatḥ, in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate). ﴿أَقْسَمْتُمْ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿لا يَنالُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ﴾: an imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the hāʾ is its object and the name of Majesty its agent; the clause has no grammatical position, being the response to the oath, and لا is negative with no governing effect. ﴿ادْخُلُوا﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its agent and ﴿الْجَنَّةَ﴾ its object; the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl) of an omitted verb: "Allah says to them: enter the Garden ...". ﴿لا خَوْفٌ﴾: لا is negative, and [خوف] is a nominative mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted khabar, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَلا أَنْتُمْ﴾: أنتم is a detached pronoun in the position of [the nominative as] mubtadaʾ, and لا is negative; the clause ﴿تَحْزَنُونَ﴾ is its khabar, and the nominal clause ولا أنتم ... is conjoined ...

daas-irab:50-50.t:
﴿وَنادى أَصْحابُ النَّارِ أَصْحابَ الْجَنَّةِ﴾: a past verb; the first أصحاب is its fāʿil (agent) and the second أصحاب its object; النار is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) and الجنة is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنْ﴾: lightened from anna, or explicative. ﴿أَفِيضُوا﴾: an imperative verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun علينا are attached. ﴿مِنَ الْماءِ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) أفيضوا. ﴿أَوْ﴾: conjunction. ﴿مِمَّا﴾: composed of مِن and the relative ما, and the verbal clause ﴿رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿قالُوا﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: inna, and the name of Majesty is its noun; the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause ﴿حَرَّمَهُما﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate). ﴿عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ﴾: attached to the verb before them.

daas-irab:144-144.t: ﴿قالَ﴾: the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿يا مُوسى﴾: the one addressed (munādā), a single proper noun. ﴿إِنِّي﴾: inna and its noun. ﴿اصْطَفَيْتُكَ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna. The clause of inna, its noun and its khabar is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿عَلَى النَّاسِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿بِرِسالاتِي﴾: a genitive (majrūr) noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person; the yāʾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to اصطفيتك. ﴿وَبِكَلامِي﴾: conjoined (ʿaṭf). ﴿فَخُذْ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition). ﴿خذ﴾: an imperative. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. The clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied non-jussive condition: "if that is so, then take what I have given you". ﴿آتَيْتُكَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the kāf is its mafʿūl; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿وَكُنْ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperative verb, its noun omitted, its implied form being "أنت". ﴿مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to its omitted khabar; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:145-145.t:
﴿وَكَتَبْنا﴾: a past verb, to which each of the prepositional phrases ﴿لَهُ﴾ and ﴿فِي الْأَلْواحِ، مِنْ كُلِّ..﴾ is attached (mutaʿalliq); and نا is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). The clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿مَوْعِظَةً﴾: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿وَتَفْصِيلًا﴾: conjoined. ﴿لِكُلِّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to تفصيلا. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَخُذْها﴾: an imperative verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis of an implied condition.
The fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿بِقُوَّةٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خذها; the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied non-jussive condition. ﴿وَأْمُرْ قَوْمَكَ﴾:
an imperative verb and its mafʿūl; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, and the kāf is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿يَأْخُذُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the command (jawāb al-ṭalab), the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil.
﴿بِأَحْسَنِها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يأخذوا; the clause is the object of the imperative verb أأمر. «[Translator's note: so in the source, "أأمر"; presumably the verb أْمُرْ is meant.]» ﴿سَأُرِيكُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the fāʿil is "أنت" «[Translator's note: so in the source; the speaker here is the first person, so the implied fāʿil would be أنا.]», and the kāf is its mafʿūl; the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural. ﴿دارَ﴾: its second mafʿūl; the underlying form is "مصير دار الفاسقين" (the end of the abode of the transgressors).
﴿الْفاسِقِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:146-146.t: ﴿سَأَصْرِفُ عَنْ آياتِيَ﴾: an imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: the relative noun is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنا"; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿يَتَكَبَّرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and fāʿil. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يتكبرون; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِغَيْرِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿الْحَقِّ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَإِنْ﴾: conditional. ﴿يَرَوْا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn, because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the wāw is the fāʿil. And ﴿كُلَّ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿آيَةٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لا يُؤْمِنُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and لا is negating, with no governing effect. ﴿بِها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb before them; the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a condition not joined to the fāʾ or to the إذا of surprise. ﴿وَإِنْ يَرَوْا سَبِيلَ الرُّشْدِ لا يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلًا﴾: the i'rab of the beginning of the verse has preceded; لا يتخذوه سبيلا: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its two mafʿūls; the clause has no grammatical position, like the one before it. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the lām is for distance and the kāf is a particle of address. ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ كَذَّبُوا﴾: أن and what follows it are, by interpretation, a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive governed by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَكانُوا﴾: kāna and its noun. ﴿عَنْها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar ﴿غافِلِينَ﴾; the clause is conjoined to the khabar clause كذبوا.

daas-irab:147-147.t:
﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَلِقاءِ﴾: conjoined. ﴿الْآخِرَةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿حَبِطَتْ أَعْمالُهُمْ﴾: a past verb and fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ الذين.
﴿هَلْ﴾: an interrogative particle conveying negation. ﴿يُجْزَوْنَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the passive, and the wāw is its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), which is the first object. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun in the position of the accusative as second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿كانُوا﴾: kāna, and the wāw is its noun; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; and the clause ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ is in the position of the accusative as its khabar.

daas-irab:148-148.t:
﴿وَاتَّخَذَ قَوْمُ﴾: a past verb and fāʿil (agent). ﴿مُوسى﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) اتخذ; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿عِجْلًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿جَسَداً﴾: badal (substitute), accusative. ﴿لَهُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿خُوارٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as a ṣifa (adjective) of جسدا.
﴿أَلَمْ يَرَوْا﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; لم is a jussive particle; يروا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنَّهُ﴾: أن, and the hāʾ is its noun. ﴿لا يُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is "هو", and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl; the mīm is for the masculine plural, and لا is negating; the clause is in the position of the nominative as khabar of أن; and أن with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يروا.
﴿وَلا يَهْدِيهِمْ سَبِيلًا﴾: an imperfect verb and its two objects, and لا is negating; the clause is conjoined. ﴿اتَّخَذُوهُ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, with its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is resumptive, and the clause كانوا ظالمين is conjoined.

daas-irab:149-149.t:
﴿وَلَمَّا﴾: adverbial (ẓarfiyya) and conditional. ﴿سُقِطَ﴾: a past verb in the passive. ﴿فِي أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾: a genitive (majrūr) noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, its appearance prevented by heaviness; the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَرَأَوْا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied on the alif that was deleted because of the meeting of two sukūns, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿أَنَّهُمْ﴾: أن and its noun, and the clause ﴿قَدْ ضَلُّوا﴾ is in the position of the nominative as its khabar (predicate). أن with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of رأوا. ﴿قالُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿لَئِنْ﴾: the lām prepares for an oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam), and إن is conditional. ﴿لَمْ﴾: a jussive particle.
﴿يَرْحَمْنا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and its mafʿūl (object), and ﴿رَبُّنا﴾ is its fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَيَغْفِرْ﴾: conjoined. ﴿لَنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يغفر. ﴿لَنَكُونَنَّ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the lām occurs in the answer to the oath; its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "نحن"; the clause has no grammatical position as the answer to the oath. The apodosis of the condition is omitted because the answer to the oath indicates it. ﴿مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of the incomplete verb.

daas-irab:150-150.t: ﴿وَلَمَّا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لما is the temporal (ḥīniyya) conditional لمّا. ﴿رَجَعَ مُوسى إِلى قَوْمِهِ﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq), and موسى is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿غَضْبانَ﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَسِفاً﴾: a second ḥāl. ﴿قالَ﴾: the clause is the answer to لما, with no grammatical position. ﴿بِئْسَما﴾: a past verb for expressing blame, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿ما﴾: an indefinite qualified noun (nakira mawṣūfa), indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as tamyīz (specification). ﴿خَلَفْتُمُونِي﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn because it is attached to the vowelled tāʾ of the agent; the mīm is for the masculine plural, and the ḍamma vowel of the mīm has been lengthened into a wāw; the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ṣifa (adjective) of ما. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِي﴾: a noun, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, and the yāʾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb before them. ﴿أَعَجِلْتُمْ﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿أَمْرَ﴾: its mafʿūl. ﴿رَبِّكُمْ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿وَأَلْقَى الْأَلْواحَ﴾: a past verb and its mafʿūl, and its fāʿil is "هو"; the clause is conjoined to قال. ﴿وَأَخَذَ بِرَأْسِ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb before them. ﴿أَخِيهِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is one of the five nouns; the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿يَجُرُّهُ إِلَيْهِ﴾: an imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl; the clause is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl. ﴿قالَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿ابْنَ أُمَّ﴾: two parts, both indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as vocative (nidāʾ); or ابن is the one addressed (munādā) and أمّ is muḍāf ilayhi, genitive by the kasra implied on the deleted alif that was converted from a yāʾ; the fatḥa indicates the deleted alif, as in a munādā annexed to the yāʾ of the first person. ﴿إِنَّ الْقَوْمَ﴾: inna and its noun. ﴿اسْتَضْعَفُونِي﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of inna, and the clause إن القوم is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كادُوا﴾: kāda and its noun. ﴿يَقْتُلُونَنِي﴾: an imperfect verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is in the position of the accusative as khabar of كادوا, and the clause كادوا is conjoined. ﴿فَلا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, and لا is the prohibitive لا, governing the jussive. ﴿تُشْمِتْ بِيَ الْأَعْداءَ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and الأعداء is its mafʿūl; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun; the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and لا is prohibitive. ﴿تَجْعَلْنِي﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive; the nūn is for protection, the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "أنت". ﴿مَعَ الْقَوْمِ﴾: an adverb of place, and القوم is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾: a ṣifa, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:151-151.t:
﴿قالَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿رَبِّ﴾: the one addressed (munādā), with the vocative particle يا omitted. ﴿اغْفِرْ لِي﴾: a verb of supplication to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq), and its fāʿil is "أنت". ﴿وَلِأَخِي﴾: a noun, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, and the yāʾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition and its genitive noun are conjoined. ﴿وَأَدْخِلْنا فِي رَحْمَتِكَ﴾: a verb of supplication to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and نا is its fāʿil «[Translator's note: so in the source; نا here is the object, the fāʿil being "أنت".]»; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَأَنْتَ﴾: أنت is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿أَرْحَمُ﴾: khabar (predicate).
﴿الرَّاحِمِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:152-152.t:
﴿إِنَّ﴾: a particle resembling the verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna. ﴿اتَّخَذُوا الْعِجْلَ﴾: a past verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the second object is omitted, i.e. "اتخذوا العجل إلها" (they took the calf as a god); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿سَيَنالُهُمْ غَضَبٌ﴾: an imperfect verb, its mafʿūl and its fāʿil; the sīn is for the future, and the clause is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) غضب. ﴿وَذِلَّةٌ﴾: conjoined. ﴿وَذِلَّةٌ فِي الْحَياةِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ذلة. ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾: a ṣifa (adjective), genitive (majrūr) by the fatḥa implied on the alif. «[Translator's note: so in the source; the implied vowel would be the kasra.]» ﴿وَكَذلِكَ﴾: the kāf is a preposition, and ذا is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ṣifa of a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object): "نجزي المفترين جزاء كائنا كذلك الجزاء" (We recompense the fabricators with a recompense like that recompense). ﴿نَجْزِي﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the implied ḍamma, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "نحن". ﴿الْمُفْتَرِينَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa).

daas-irab:153-153.t:
﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa).
﴿عَمِلُوا السَّيِّئاتِ﴾: a past verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative by the kasra in place of the fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿ثُمَّ تابُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and ثم is a conjunction. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them; the clause is conjoined, and likewise the clause آمنوا. ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَغَفُورٌ﴾: inna, its noun and its khabar (predicate), and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).
And ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾: a second khabar; the clause is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ الذين.

daas-irab:154-154.t:
﴿وَلَمَّا﴾: adverbial (ẓarfiyya) and conditional, and the wāw is resumptive. ﴿سَكَتَ عَنْ مُوسَى الْغَضَبُ﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq), and الغضب is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); and the clause ﴿أَخَذَ الْأَلْواحَ﴾ has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿وَفِي نُسْخَتِها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿هُدىً﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿وَرَحْمَةٌ﴾: conjoined. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun) رحمة. ﴿هُمْ﴾: a detached nominative pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِرَبِّهِمْ﴾: the lām is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition.
﴿ربهم﴾: a noun genitive in form and accusative in position, as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يَرْهَبُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. The clause is the khabar of هم; and the clause هم لربهم يرهبون is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:155-155.t: ﴿وَاخْتارَ مُوسى﴾: a past verb and fāʿil (agent). ﴿قَوْمَهُ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative by removal of the preposition; its original form is "من قومه". The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. «[Translator's note: so in the source.]» ﴿سَبْعِينَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative by the yāʾ. ﴿رَجُلًا﴾: tamyīz (specification). ﴿لِمِيقاتِنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb اختار; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾: لما is adverbial (ẓarfiyya) and conditional, and the fāʾ is resumptive. ﴿أَخَذَتْهُمُ﴾: a past verb with the tāʾ of the feminine, and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl. ﴿الرَّجْفَةُ﴾: its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿قالَ﴾: the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to لما. ﴿رَبِّ﴾: the one addressed (munādā), annexed. The vocative clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿لَوْ﴾: a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿شِئْتَ﴾: a past verb and fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position, being the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿أَهْلَكْتَهُمْ﴾: a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾: an adverb of time, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive, because it is cut off from annexation; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb before them. ﴿وَإِيَّايَ﴾: a detached pronoun, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the hāʾ in أهلكتهم; the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿أَتُهْلِكُنا﴾: an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is "أنت"; the hamza is for interrogation. ﴿بِما﴾: ما is a relative noun, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the genitive governed by the preposition; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb. ﴿فَعَلَ السُّفَهاءُ﴾: a past verb and fāʿil. ﴿مِنَّا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from السفهاء; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا فِتْنَتُكَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); إن is negating with the meaning of ما, and إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); the clause is resumptive, together with the speech. ﴿تُضِلُّ بِها مَنْ تَشاءُ﴾: an imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and the relative noun is its mafʿūl; the clause is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl, and the clause تشاء is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿وَتَهْدِي مَنْ تَشاءُ﴾: conjoined. ﴿أَنْتَ وَلِيُّنا﴾: mubtadaʾ and khabar. ﴿فَاغْفِرْ لَنا﴾: a verb of supplication to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and its fāʿil is "أنت"; the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition). The clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied condition. ﴿وَارْحَمْنا﴾: conjoined. ﴿وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and khabar. ﴿الْغافِرِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl after the wāw of circumstance, or it is resumptive.

daas-irab:51-51.t:
﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of the genitive (majrūr) as an adjective (ṣifa) of الكافرين. ﴿اتَّخَذُوا دِينَهُمْ لَهْواً﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its two objects.
﴿وَلَعِباً﴾: conjoined, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَغَرَّتْهُمُ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥ; the tāʾ is for the feminine, the hāʾ is its object, and the mīm is for the masculine plural. ﴿الْحَياةُ﴾: agent, and ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ is a nominative adjective; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَالْيَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb ﴿نَنْساهُمْ﴾; the fāʾ is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿كَما﴾: the kāf is a preposition and ما is maṣdarī; together with the verb after it, it is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive by the kāf, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted maṣdar: "We forget them with a forgetting like their forgetting of the meeting of this Day of theirs". ﴿نَسُوا﴾:
a past verb and its agent. ﴿لِقاءَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يَوْمِهِمْ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the hāʾ is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa (annexation). ﴿هذا﴾: a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as badal (substitute) or adjective. ﴿وَما كانُوا﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the wāw is its noun; ما is maṣdarī, and the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to the preceding maṣdar: "and their being ones who reject". ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾: attached to the verb after them. The clause ﴿يَجْحَدُونَ﴾ is in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as khabar (predicate).

daas-irab:52-52.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, the lām occurs in the response to an implied oath, and قد is a particle of realization. ﴿جِئْناهُمْ﴾: a past verb; نا is its fāʿil (agent) and the hāʾ its object. ﴿بِكِتابٍ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿فَصَّلْناهُ﴾: a past verb, its agent and its object; the clause is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) as an adjective (ṣifa) of كتاب, and the clause ﴿جِئْناهُمْ﴾ has no grammatical position, being the response to the oath. ﴿عَلى عِلْمٍ﴾: attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of فصلناه, i.e., "We detailed it, comprising knowledge". ﴿هُدىً﴾: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) or ḥāl. ﴿وَرَحْمَةً﴾: conjoined. ﴿لِقَوْمٍ﴾: attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun) هدى or to رحمة. The clause ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of قوم.

daas-irab:53-53.t: ﴿هَلْ﴾: an interrogative particle. ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿تَأْوِيلَهُ﴾: its object. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction [Translator's note: so in the source; this repeats the previous item]. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb يقول. ﴿يَأْتِي تَأْوِيلُهُ﴾: an imperfect verb and its agent; the clause is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa (annexation). ﴿يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ﴾: an imperfect verb, and the relative noun is its agent. ﴿نَسُوهُ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma;
